last_run.broken_assumption: HumanityAI currently assumes that building a broad, high-quality map of problems and evidence will eventually create downstream value. If the project vanished tomorrow, however, most of today's outputs would likely be replaced by existing research/search systems and almost no real human decision would measurably change. The missing primitive is not more supply of knowledge; it is durable evidence of demand and decision pull.

strongest_ideas.name: Decision-demand ledger
strongest_ideas.idea: Add a public machine-readable ledger of real decisions, questions, or coordination bottlenecks that humans or organizations actually need help resolving. Each demand object should record the decision owner or stakeholder class at a privacy-safe level, decision deadline, alternatives under consideration, what evidence would change the decision, affected groups, uncertainty, and whether HumanityAI's work was actually used. Research tasks can then be generated from unresolved demand rather than only from a global supply-side map.
strongest_ideas.why_novel_here: Current HumanityAI work is mostly supply-first: identify important problems, collect evidence, map interventions, then hope usefulness follows. A demand ledger inverts the causal direction and gives the project a direct counterfactual test: did a concrete decision become better, faster, more evidence-grounded, or more contestable because HumanityAI existed?
strongest_ideas.expected_upside: Creates measurable counterfactual value, gives task selection real external pull, reduces impressive-but-unused research, naturally connects to the earlier decision-to-outcome lifecycle, and can reveal which parts of the world model are actually useful rather than merely complete.
failure_modes: Early demand may be unrepresentative and bias the project toward vocal or well-connected users.
Urgent visible decisions may crowd out foundational research whose value is delayed.
Demand objects can expose sensitive context if privacy is handled badly.
Users may ask for decisions HumanityAI should not influence or cannot safely support.
Optimizing for recorded use could Goodhart into shallow responsiveness instead of genuine benefit.
strongest_ideas.rights_distribution: Record affected groups and who gets to define the decision. Do not treat the requester's objective as morally exhaustive. Preserve the option to refuse or reframe coercive, rights-violating, privacy-sensitive, or inappropriate requests.
strongest_ideas.reversibility: High if prototyped with synthetic or historical demand objects before accepting live submissions.
strongest_ideas.falsifiable_next_test: Create three synthetic or historical demand objects from decisions already discussed in HumanityAI's evidence domains. Compare task selection and output against the current backlog. Keep the concept only if it changes at least one research priority or reveals evidence that would matter to a decision but is invisible in the current problem-map workflow.

strongest_ideas.name: Proof-of-use feedback instead of repository activity
strongest_ideas.idea: For selected outputs, track a small chain of downstream evidence: requested -> delivered -> read/reused -> decision influenced or not -> later outcome when observable. A null result ('useful-looking analysis changed nothing') is first-class evidence and should reduce confidence in similar work classes.
strongest_ideas.why_novel_here: EVALUATION.md calls for counterfactual value and external validation, but there is not yet a concrete object tying an artifact to actual use or non-use. This converts 'utility' from a self-assessment dimension into observable feedback.
strongest_ideas.expected_upside: Provides a reality-based signal for recursive task selection, identifies dead-end work classes, and gives HumanityAI a reason to stop producing artifacts that nobody needs.
failure_modes: Use is not the same as benefit.
Tracking can become invasive or burdensome.
Popular outputs can dominate neglected but important work.
strongest_ideas.rights_distribution: Use only voluntary/public feedback; do not instrument people covertly. Keep non-use as neutral evidence rather than blaming users.
strongest_ideas.reversibility: High as an additive experimental registry.
strongest_ideas.falsifiable_next_test: Define a minimal proof-of-use schema and retrospectively classify three existing HumanityAI outputs as no observed use / internal use / externally evidenced use. If every record collapses to speculation, that itself is evidence the project currently lacks a real impact-feedback channel.

strongest_ideas.name: Explicit pull-versus-exploration portfolio
strongest_ideas.idea: Split future work into two visibly different portfolios: demand-pulled work tied to concrete decision needs, and exploration work justified by neglectedness or option value. Evaluate them differently rather than forcing all research through one impact heuristic.
strongest_ideas.why_novel_here: A pure demand-first system would overfit current users, while the current supply-first system risks irrelevance. Treating both as separate portfolios preserves long-horizon discovery while adding accountability to real-world usefulness.
strongest_ideas.expected_upside: Prevents the demand-ledger idea from becoming a new Goodhart target and makes tradeoffs between immediate usefulness and foundational exploration explicit.
failure_modes: Exploration can become a loophole for low-value work.
Demand work can dominate because its feedback is faster.
strongest_ideas.rights_distribution: Exploration priorities should continue to account for neglected populations whose needs may not appear in incoming demand.
strongest_ideas.falsifiable_next_test: Classify the current high-value backlog into pull-capable versus exploration work and see whether this exposes any tasks whose justification is only 'it seems important' without a plausible use or option-value case.

rejected_or_deferred: Immediately solicit real organizations or policymakers for decision requests: potentially high value, but external outreach requires human review and the internal demand schema should first be tested on historical/synthetic cases.
Make user demand the sole task-selection criterion: this would systematically neglect voiceless, future, or poorly organized populations and would violate the project's broader mission.
Use clicks, stars, traffic, or downloads as proof of use: these are weak attention metrics and can reward popularity without decision value.
Replace the global problem map with a request queue: the map remains useful as exploration infrastructure and as a check against narrow incoming demand.
last_run.recommended_next_test: Prototype three historical/synthetic decision-demand objects and a minimal proof-of-use field set without changing protected policy. Compare whether they materially alter task selection or reveal decision-relevant evidence gaps that current supply-first research misses.

notes: Frontier state records conceptual experiments, not authority. Ideas may exceed current execution permissions; human-review boundaries remain governed by security/policy.json.
